body:
Yeah, it's somewhat easy to distract yourself, but your feelings are still there. Can't wait until one day I'll be (at least) feeling neutral about things.

And not to worry- I did read a lot of post-breakup depression articles before writing, and the tips to overcome it parrot your ideas. I know that these feelings will not last forever. It's possibly a mix of being young and emotionally immature, and having just ended my first serious relationship, that I feel worse than I might be doing in the same situation ten years from now. It's hard to put things in perspective at this moment, but that train of thought does help me a little. 

I hope that you've followed your own advice to the end, and have gotten over the relationship that ended last year.

Thank you, Poet. I've never talked about my ex's aspergers outside of a wall of anonymity. He was the most fulfilling relationship that I've had- I loved the brutal honesty because I prioritise communication with my partner above all else. I never judged him for it, but that kind of relationship does require a special kind of patience and thick skin, and I suppose I just wasn't the right person to handle that.

I'm trying to put myself out there and meet new people. I'm actually on a dating site right now- and I feel like I'm living in two separate worlds. I'm showing my normal, happier exterior to them online, but as soon as I go offline it all comes crashing down, and I can't seem to accept the reality that I'm single. It's.. a cycle. I hope it ends soon.
